item.title: China's central bank to raise forex reserve requirement ratio to keep yuan stable
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
China's central bank to raise forex reserve requirement ratio to keep yuan stable BEIJING, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- China's central bank on Tuesday announced that it will raise the foreign exchange (forex) reserve requirement ratio for financial institutions by 2 percentage points, the first increase in nearly five years, in a move that is expected to ease the upward pressure on the Chinese currency renminbi and stabilize market expectations. The People's Bank of China (PBOC) said in a statement that it will raise the forex reserve requirement ratio from 4 to 6 percent from Nov. 15 this year. A macro-prudential management tool in the forex market, the forex reserve requirement ratio refers to the share of foreign currency deposits that financial institutions must hold at the PBOC. An increase tightens U.S. dollar liquidity and eases upward pressure on the renminbi, or the yuan, and a cut eases downward pressure on the yuan. The latest move comes as the yuan has broadly strengthened this year. In the first nine months of this year, the yuan appreciated by a cumulative 4.2 percent against the U.S. dollar. The pace has accelerated since October, with the onshore yuan exchange rate strengthening for 14 consecutive trading days from October 14. Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank, said that the increase in the ratio will help promote supply-demand balance in the forex market and curb a self-fulfilling cycle in which expectations of yuan appreciation drive further gains in the yuan. He noted that raising the ratio is an open and transparent market-based measure, and that the adjustment sends a policy signal to the market that the central bank will stabilize market expectations and keep the yuan exchange rate basically stable at a reasonable and balanced level. The PBOC has adjusted the ratio multiple times. In 2021, it raised the ratio twice to 9 percent. From 2022 to 2023, it lowered the ratio three times to the current 4 percent. Following the announcement, the offshore yuan exchange rate fell against the U.S. dollar. Data from the China Foreign Exchange Trade System showed that as of 4:30 p.m., the onshore yuan spot exchange rate closed at 6.6765 against the U.S. dollar, weakening by 307 pips from the previous trading day. In October, the PBOC issued its policy stance on the yuan exchange rate, saying that it will focus on preventing sharp short-term fluctuations in the exchange rate, especially sharp short-term depreciation that could affect financial stability. The PBOC does not preset a target level for the exchange rate, but if the exchange rate fluctuates sharply in the short term and the market shows herd behavior and irrational expectations, it will introduce market-based measures to prevent short-term disruptive overshooting of the exchange rate, it said. Ming Ming, chief economist at CITIC Securities, said the PBOC's move will freeze about 20 billion to 25 billion U.S. dollars of forex liquidity at the bank level and promote supply-demand balance in the domestic forex market. item.title: China's resolve to safeguard sovereignty, territorial integrity remains unwavering, says FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
China's resolve to safeguard sovereignty, territorial integrity remains unwavering, says FM BEIJING, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- China's resolve to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity and achieve national reunification remains unwavering, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Tuesday. During a phone conversation with Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, urged the Philippine side to faithfully implement its one-China policy and exercise prudence in its words and actions on maritime issues. Noting that China-Philippines relations are facing malicious interference at present, Wang said that a few Philippine politicians, out of political prejudice and self-interest, have repeatedly attacked and smeared China. Such deeds crossed China's red lines, politicized normal economic, trade and people-to-people exchanges, and infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese personnel and institutions in the Philippines, Wang said. Such deeds are irrational and intolerable, and damaging to the Philippines' own international image, Wang said, adding that Manila should exercise greater restraint over the individuals concerned and ensure that its policy toward China reflects a rational and unified voice. For her part, Lazaro said that the Philippines attaches great importance to its relations with China and hopes to develop a stable and predictable bilateral relationship. Given the challenges that countries currently face in areas such as economy and energy, communication between the Philippines and China is conducive to managing differences, improving bilateral ties, and promoting regional peace and stability, Lazaro said. The Philippines, she added, remains committed to the one-China policy, a position that will not change, and is also prepared to address maritime and other issues appropriately through dialogue and consultation. As the ASEAN rotating chair, the Philippines appreciates and looks forward to China playing a greater role in advancing the ASEAN-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to achieve further results, she said. The two sides reached basic consensus on improving and developing China-Philippines relations. They agreed that healthy and stable bilateral relations serve the interests of both sides and meet regional expectations, and they agreed to maintain diplomatic dialogue to that end. They agreed that the two countries should work together to eliminate all internal and external interference, and oppose any malicious provocation or behavior aimed at undermining their diplomatic engagement. They also agreed that both sides should responsibly manage their differences, stabilize the situation and seek to expand their shared interests. Wang and Lazaro also exchanged views on the leaders' meetings on East Asian cooperation to be held in the Philippines, as well as the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting to be held subsequently in Shenzhen, China. item.title: Taiwan has no right to join Interpol: mainland spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
Taiwan has no right to join Interpol: mainland spokesperson BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- Taiwan, as part of China, does not have the right to become an Interpol member, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office said on Wednesday. Spokesperson Zhu Fenglian made the remarks at a regular press conference in response to a media query about the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' call for international support for Taiwan's inclusion in Interpol, from which the island has been excluded for decades. Interpol, an intergovernmental organization for police cooperation in combating crime, has 196 member countries, each hosting a National Central Bureau. "The participation of the Taiwan region in activities of international organizations must be in accordance with the one-China principle. This has been our consistent and clear position," Zhu said. The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Zhu noted that China and Interpol have already made proper arrangements for the Taiwan region to participate in cooperation and activities under the Interpol framework. Police authorities in the Taiwan region have unimpeded channels for information sharing and cooperation on cases with Interpol National Central Bureaus in all member countries, she added. The DPP authorities have been trying to deceive people on the island through repeated political manipulation over Taiwan's participation in international organizations, but their attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" via provocations will inevitably fail, the spokesperson said. item.title: 7th World Media Summit to kick off in Beijing to boost media cooperation in intelligent age
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
7th World Media Summit to kick off in Beijing to boost media cooperation in intelligent age BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- The 7th World Media Summit, which is co-hosted by Xinhua News Agency and the People's Government of Beijing Municipality, is to be held from Nov. 5 to 9 in Beijing. According to the summit secretariat, under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action", the summit will bring together nearly 500 delegates from nearly 330 mainstream media outlets, think tanks, government departments and international organizations from 112 countries and regions around the world. Delegates will exchange views on topics including "AI for all and the transformation of global media," "media dialogue and cooperation for a safer world," "AI-enabled communication for expanding exchanges among civilizations," "AI+ and the future of global communication governance" and "the Beijing approach: decoding Chinese modernization." They will also tour Beijing on the sidelines of the summit. The mechanism of the World Media Summit was initiated in 2009 and is an important global platform for high-end media exchange and cooperation. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China issues guidelines to boost consumption, investment through infrastructure upgrades
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
China issues guidelines to boost consumption, investment through infrastructure upgrades BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- China has issued new guidelines to strengthen consumption-related infrastructure, aiming to stimulate consumer spending, expand effective investment and foster a mutually reinforcing relationship between consumption and investment. The guidelines, jointly issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and other government departments, outline measures to upgrade urban and rural commercial facilities, improve facilities for service consumption and travel-related consumption, strengthen distribution networks and develop infrastructure for new forms of consumption. Under the guidelines, China will promote the digital transformation of urban and rural marketplaces and advance upgrades in older shopping districts through cultural and creative businesses, night markets, trendy retail outlets and immersive experiences. The guidelines also encourage the development of fitness centers and water sports facilities based on local conditions, as well as wider use of smart home products and intelligent monitoring devices. To improve travel-related consumption infrastructure, China will support the expansion and renovation of parking facilities in commercial districts, shopping complexes, tourist attractions and cultural and tourism consumption hubs where parking capacity is insufficient. To develop infrastructure for new forms of consumption, the guidelines call for expanding the coverage of 5G networks, gigabit optical networks, the Internet of Things and cloud computing across shopping districts, marketplaces and tourist attractions to enhance connectivity, smart services and data sharing. Efforts will also be made to promote green marketplaces, shopping districts, malls and hotels, and to encourage energy-saving upgrades and carbon emission reductions at consumption venues. The guidelines come as China has already rolled out a series of measures to stimulate consumption, strengthen domestic demand and support broader economic growth amid external uncertainties. In July, China released its first five-year plan dedicated exclusively to expanding consumption. The plan aims to unlock the full potential of the country's super-large market, optimize the consumption structure and improve people's livelihoods through targeted measures. Earlier data showed that in the first three quarters of 2026, China's total retail sales of goods and services rose 2.6 percent year on year. Domestic consumption contributed nearly half of economic growth in the period, adding 2.1 percentage points to GDP growth. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: On Mount Tai, a tough test for China's robots
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
On Mount Tai, a tough test for China's robots A robot competes in a climbing competition on Mount Tai in Taian, east China's Shandong Province, Nov. 2, 2026. The first world robot Mount Tai climbing competition was held in Taian on Monday, bringing together nearly 90 teams on Mount Tai's historic hiking trails. (Xinhua/Zhu Zheng) JINAN, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- Carrying eggs, instant noodles and bottled water on their backs, robotic dogs began climbing Mount Tai in east China's Shandong Province on Monday, setting off at two-minute intervals on a challenging 3.9-kilometer route involving more than 3,100 steps. The route took them along steep slopes and uneven stone steps, some barely wide enough for half an adult foot. The climb was part of a robot competition that brought together companies, universities and research teams from across China. For their developers, the mountain offered a chance to test technologies in a demanding real-world setting and explore their potential applications in everyday life. The competition assessed not only climbing speed, but also the ability to transport cargo safely. Items included fragile goods, such as eggs and watermelons, as well as irregularly shaped objects, such as thermos flasks. Damage to delicate cargo would cost points. "Eggs are fragile. We have to consider how to carry them steadily up the mountain while minimizing breakage," said Li Jinxiang, a marketing manager at GENISOM AI, one of the participating manufacturers. The task was familiar on Mount Tai, where human porters have long carried supplies up steep stone steps for tourists. Robotic dogs have already begun taking on some of that work, hauling supplies uphill and garbage downhill. But the terrain remains difficult even for machines built to negotiate rough ground. Chen Xiyun, marketing manager at Unitree Robotics, said the mountain's steps varied widely in height and width. Rain made them slippery, while steep slopes and crowds of tourists added to the challenge. Such conditions, he said, made Mount Tai an ideal testing ground for robots intended for practical use. A robot competes in a climbing competition on Mount Tai in Taian, east China's Shandong Province, Nov. 2, 2026. The first world robot Mount Tai climbing competition was held in Taian on Monday, bringing together nearly 90 teams on Mount Tai's historic hiking trails. (Xinhua/Xu Suhui) While robotic dogs are being tested for carrying heavy loads, wearable robots are finding another use: helping people walk. The competition also included an exoskeleton-assisted climbing event to assess how well wearable devices could reduce the physical effort of climbing the mountain. Similar technology is finding applications in rehabilitation, outdoor recreation and fitness. MileBot, a robotics company in east China's Anhui Province, has developed a walking-assistance exoskeleton weighing just 1.8 kilograms, and about 2 kilograms with its battery. The company initially manufactured medical devices, and its exoskeleton products have been used in several hospitals for lower-limb rehabilitation. It has since expanded into industrial robotics and wearable smart devices. Dai Hui, the company's regional manager for east China, said the device could recognize different walking patterns, including the shorter steps taken by some older people, and adjust its assistance accordingly. It can also provide assistance to either leg, a feature Dai said could help improve walking patterns in people with partial paralysis following a stroke. Another setting adds resistance, making walking on level ground feel more like climbing uphill. Dai said the mode was intended for physical training. China is seeking to expand such applications under its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). But the competition on Mount Tai also showed the challenges that remain. Some robotic dogs stumbled or bumped into walls. Several humanoid robots lost their balance, with some falling shortly after setting off. Others still depended heavily on human operators. Liu Wenqiang, vice president of China Center for Information Industry Development, said testing robots in real environments helped manufacturers collect data to improve their products. The data collected on Mount Tai could also help developers prepare robots for other tasks. Wang Yani, a brand strategy executive at Universal Ubiquitous AI Co., Ltd., said the data could support future applications in power facility inspections, security patrols and emergency rescue operations. "We hope robots can help people with work that is dirty, tiring and physically demanding," she said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Hainan FTP law implementation yields positive results: report
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
Hainan FTP law implementation yields positive results: report A drone photo shows cruises sailing near the Phoenix Island in Sanya, south China's Hainan Province, Oct. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhao Yingquan) BEIJING, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- The implementation of the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP) Law has yielded positive results, with island-wide special customs operations progressing steadily, according to a law enforcement inspection report submitted to the 25th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress (NPC) on Tuesday. The report, from an inspection team of the NPC Standing Committee, said the Hainan FTP's role in promoting opening up and cooperation has become increasingly evident, with its demonstration effect continuing to grow. Hainan FTP's law-based environment has continued to improve, with a preliminary policy and institutional framework in place, according to the report. South China's island province of Hainan formulated a special plan for supporting regulations for the Hainan Free Trade Port Law for the 2021-2025 period and introduced 60 regulations, including those related to intellectual property protection and fair competition. The province has established a free trade port intellectual property court and an international commercial dispute resolution center, advanced reforms in ad hoc arbitration and commercial mediation, and put in place a one-stop, diversified dispute resolution mechanism integrating mediation, arbitration and litigation. The report noted that difficulties and problems remain in implementing the law and the mechanisms for trade liberalization and facilitation. To further advance the implementation of the law, it proposed recommendations in four areas, including improving the policy and institutional framework, further unlocking the benefits of fiscal and tax reforms, optimizing the development environment, and strengthening institutional safeguards. In June 2021, China adopted the Hainan Free Trade Port Law, which stipulates that the development of the port should focus on trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, be supported by the free, orderly, safe and convenient cross-border flows of various factors of production and a modern industrial system, and be underpinned by special tax arrangements, an efficient social governance system and a comprehensive system for the rule of law. On Dec. 18, 2025, China launched island-wide special customs operations in the Hainan Free Trade Port, expanding the share of tariff lines eligible for zero-tariff treatment on qualifying imports from 21 percent to 74 percent. Goods shipped onward from Hainan to the Chinese mainland remain subject to separate customs controls. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Unlocking a vast market for the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
Xi Focus: Unlocking a vast market for the world SHANGHAI, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- After a journey of more than two months across continents and oceans, machinery from WFL Millturn Technologies cleared customs in Shanghai last month for this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE), carrying the Austrian manufacturer's hopes of expanding further into Chinese and wider Asia-Pacific markets. "I don't see any good reason why we will not be successful in China in the upcoming decades," said WFL Managing Director Stefan Hackl. His company will make a double debut: its first appearance at the import expo after more than 20 years in the Chinese market, and the Asian debut of its brand-new machine tool. The company's confidence is rooted in part in the vision behind the CIIE, an initiative championed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has personally planned and steered its development. Designed to give overseas businesses greater access to the vast and growing Chinese market, the expo has increasingly turned China's development into opportunities for the world. Now in its ninth year, the CIIE has become a regular fixture on the global trade calendar. Running from Nov. 5 to 10, the expo will bring together 4,142 overseas exhibitors, including more than 2,000 first-time participants like WFL. In the weeks leading up to the expo, shipments from around the world continued to arrive in Shanghai, bringing in a diverse range of products, from Peruvian bananas and French tires to Australian coffee and Kazakh ice cream, all ready to meet buyers at the event. As the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports, the CIIE offers a compelling response to rising protectionism and trade barriers. Rather than viewing trade as a competition for a limited share of global demand, it seeks to make the world economic pie bigger by creating opportunities for businesses and economies to grow together. "Our aim is to turn the China market into a market for the world, a market shared by all, and a market accessible to all," Xi has said. "This way, we will be able to bring more positive energy to the global community." A PROMISE KEPT In his keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the first CIIE in 2018, Xi said the expo is "an important decision made by China to pursue a new round of high-level opening-up, and is China's major initiative to still widen market access to the rest of the world." "China's initiative to expand imports is not a choice of expediency. It is a future-oriented step taken to embrace the world and promote common development," Xi said, pledging that the event would be held annually and "feature good performance, good results and continued success in the years to come." Eight years on, the CIIE has grown into a premier global platform for trade, investment and cultural exchanges, connecting businesses, innovators and consumers from around the world. The promise of an annual expo with lasting results has been borne out by its growth. Past editions have drawn more than 180 countries, regions and international organizations and seen more than 3,400 new products, technologies and services make their debut, while cumulative intended deals have exceeded 580 billion U.S. dollars, according to the organizer. "The CIIE is far more than a trade show," said Jérôme Vanachter, president of Lesaffre Greater China. The French yeast maker is back for a ninth consecutive edition this year. Calling the expo a "market-intelligence hub," Vanachter said the CIIE helps turn market insights into products. Past expos have also seen Xi announce a series of opening-up measures, including advancing the development of pilot free trade zones and the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP), continuously trimming the negative lists for foreign investment, and expanding the opening of telecommunications, healthcare and other services. These pledges were followed by concrete actions. In November 2024, China removed the last two manufacturing-related restrictions from its national negative list for foreign investment. Last December, the Hainan FTP launched island-wide special customs operations, a milestone in China's drive for high-standard opening-up. "Today, the CIIE has become a showcase of China's new development paradigm, a platform for high-standard opening-up, and a public good for the whole world," Xi said at the fifth edition of the event in 2022. The role of the CIIE in China's opening-up agenda is expected to continue in the years ahead. In its five-year development blueprint for the 2026-2030 period, the country has called for expanding imports and continuing to hold the CIIE and other major trade fairs, including the Canton Fair in south China, while strengthening trade-promotion platforms. A MARKET SHARED BY ALL "Economic globalization represents the trend of history," Xi said at the second CIIE in 2019, likening it to the world's great rivers -- the Yangtze, the Nile, the Amazon and the Danube, which all "surge forward in relentless flow, and nothing can stop their mighty movement." China has been translating this vision into action by opening wider. Quality products from an increasing number of countries are finding a foothold in the Chinese market, generating profits for businesses, wages for workers and tax revenues in their home countries. For 17 consecutive years, China has remained the world's second-largest importer. Also in the first three quarters of 2026, the country's imports rose 22.3 percent year on year, significantly outpacing export growth. "The vastly huge China market is the most promising in the world," Xi noted at the third CIIE in 2020, citing the country's huge population and vast middle-income group. The country's retail sales of consumer goods surpassed 50 trillion yuan (about 7.44 trillion U.S. dollars) for the first time last year, and are expected to grow by another 10 trillion yuan over the next five years. The appeal of the Chinese market is reflected in the growing participation of global businesses in the CIIE, which has attracted a record number of more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders this year. In terms of exhibition space, U.S. exhibitors lead for the eighth consecutive year, occupying more than 50,000 square meters, while companies from Germany, the United Kingdom and France also rank among the top participants. Over 480 products are set to make their global, Asian or China debut at the event, the highest number in history, underscoring the Chinese market's growing role as a launchpad for global innovation. Under Xi's leadership, China has also sought to make the opportunities offered by its market more accessible to developing countries. For years, the CIIE has provided free exhibition booths to exhibitors from the world's least developed countries. This year, according to the organizer, the exhibition area for African businesses is set to increase steadily, while the space allocated for free booths for the least developed countries will expand by 17 percent. An official delegation from Cote d'Ivoire will make its first appearance at the CIIE's business exhibition this year, showcasing cocoa, coffee, cashews and kola nuts. In May, a zero-tariff policy took effect on imports from all 53 African countries with which China has diplomatic relations. "We are very happy to participate for the first time," said Rami Koné, an official with the country's export agency. "This will be a good opportunity to showcase Cote d'Ivoire to the world." "Of the problems confronting the world economy, none can be resolved by a single country alone," Xi once said. "We must all put the common good of humanity first rather than place one's own interest above the common interest of all." As Xi has pledged, China will continue to open its arms to the world, offering countries greater opportunities for market access, investment and growth. "Together, we can achieve development for all," he has said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
